stories.title: Burnham pledges 'tough decisions' as UK inflation hits 3.1%
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is ready to take difficult decisions to keep the UK economy on track, after data showed inflation rising to 3.1% in August — a five-month high — raising questions ahead of the October 28 budget.

stories.title: Government to function normally while Burnham on holiday, No 10 confirms
stories.summary: Downing Street confirmed Andy Burnham's government will continue to operate normally while the prime minister takes a short break, with senior ministers holding the fort.

stories.title: NATO Secretary General meets PM Burnham in London
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte visited the United Kingdom and held talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham, with defence spending and the UK's commitments discussed.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 'A critical moment': Concerns UK is not up to speed on AI risks after DSIT scrapped
stories.summary: The Guardian reports growing concern that Burnham's focus on domestic priorities, combined with his scrapping of DSIT on day one, has caused AI safety and regulation to fall off the government's radar. Critics warn of a governance vacuum in the critical AI policy space.

stories.title: 🤖 Digital ID officials 'being redeployed to other government priorities'
stories.summary: PublicTechnology reports that civil servants who worked on the now-cancelled national digital ID scheme are being moved to other government priorities, signalling the end of that agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 NHS signs £200m AI and digital deal to upgrade screening services
stories.summary: The NHS has agreed a major £200m deal to deploy AI and digital tools across its cancer and clinical screening services, one of the largest NHS tech contracts of the year.

stories.title: 🤖 AI to reduce paperwork burden on business — UKAuthority
stories.summary: The government has announced plans to use AI to streamline corporate reporting requirements, with ministers saying it will reduce the administrative burden on businesses.

stories.title: 🏗️ Burnham government strips back procurement rules to prioritise British jobs
stories.summary: The Burnham government has replaced wide-ranging green and social procurement targets, instead instructing firms bidding for public contracts to prove they are creating UK jobs — a significant shift framing procurement as a tool for reindustrialisation.

stories.title: 🏢 MoJ signs £100m BT 'bridging' deal to maintain prisoners' telephony
stories.summary: The Ministry of Justice has signed a £100m 'bridging' contract with BT to maintain telephony systems for prisons while a longer-term solution is procured — a significant vendor signal in public sector connectivity.

stories.title: 📄 Research Report — Building No. 10 North (re-state.co.uk)
stories.summary: Re:State think tank proposes a detailed blueprint for Burnham's 'Number 10 North' — envisioning it as a 'testbed for a radically different approach to governance' with four core units and a PM Transformation Directorate. Key risks: symbolism without impact, insufficient scale, and that the actual building won't be ready until 2032.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: NHS Reform Bill enters committee stage in Commons: NHS England abolition debated
stories.summary: The landmark NHS Reform Bill entered detailed committee stage, with MPs debating the abolition of NHS England, changes to Integrated Care Boards, and the proposed Single Patient Record. Significant amendments are expected on procurement, women's health and workforce.

stories.title: E-petition debate on public ownership of water held in Commons
stories.summary: An e-petition calling for a referendum on the public ownership of water was debated in the House of Commons on 14 September 2026, reflecting growing public interest in nationalisation of utilities under the Burnham government.

stories.title: Burnham faces PMQs with Badenoch and faces first conference season as PM
stories.summary: PM Burnham has faced his first two sessions of PMQs since taking office on 20 July 2026. Parliament is now on conference recess, returning after party conferences conclude.

stories.title: Trade unions, MPs and donors urge Burnham to revisit party funding rules
stories.summary: Labour figures including trade union leaders, MPs and major donors are pressing Burnham to reform internal party funding rules, with some warning that 'Britain cannot let billionaire donors buy our democracy' — echoing tensions over Reform UK's donations.

stories.title: Labour's plan for 'reindustrialisation': Burnham hosts business leaders at No 10
stories.summary: Burnham hosted entrepreneurs, business leaders and local mayors at Downing Street to launch his 'reindustrialise Britain' agenda, pitching the government as a 'partner for growth' and pledging a culture shift in how Britain does business.

stories.title: Burnham government pauses early prisoner release scheme amid concerns
stories.summary: The Burnham government halted its planned early prisoner release scheme that had been due to start in September, following safety concerns — a significant reversal of a key criminal justice policy inherited from the Starmer era.

stories.title: The Guardian: Badenoch's economic plan 'stuck in Tory comfort zone'
stories.summary: A Guardian editorial argues that Kemi Badenoch's newly unveiled economic proposals fail to offer a distinctive break from Tory orthodoxy, leaving the Conservatives struggling to differentiate from both Labour and Reform UK.

stories.title: Badenoch gives keynote speech on defence, seeks to reclaim patriotism agenda
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch gave a high-profile speech on UK defence at a central London event, seeking to reassert Tory credentials on national security as polling shows Labour and Reform ahead.

stories.title: Badenoch faces criticism over defence of ex-neo-Nazi in 'weird week'
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch faced sustained criticism after defending a man with a far-right extremist past, described as a 'weird week' in which she was accused of aping Reform on policy and purging centrists from the party.

stories.title: Lib Dem conference underway in Brighton — Davey claims 'moral responsibility' to block Reform
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrats' annual conference opened in Brighton (19-22 September 2026), with leader Ed Davey declaring the party has a 'moral responsibility' to block Nigel Farage's Reform UK and positioning the Lib Dems as the anti-Reform firewall.

stories.title: Lib Dems begin work on snap election manifesto amid polling concerns
stories.summary: The party has started drafting a new manifesto in preparation for a possible snap election, as Davey acknowledged frustration among MPs that the party's message risks being lost amid the Labour-Reform battle.

stories.title: Council leader warns Lib Dems are 'sleepwalking to irrelevance' under Davey
stories.summary: An internal critic — a senior council leader — said the Lib Dems risk becoming irrelevant unless they sharpen their political identity, raising pressure on Davey to show a more radical side at conference.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Farage says £72m Reform donations are 'compliant with the law today'
stories.summary: Nigel Farage defended £72m in donations to Reform UK — including £36m from cryptocurrency billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo — saying all donations are '100% compliant with the law today'. The government is seeking to cap expat donations at £100,000/year backdated to 25 March 2026.

stories.title: Reform officials suspended after Channel 4 undercover donations investigation
stories.summary: Reform UK suspended party officials following a Channel 4 News undercover investigation into the party's fundraising practices. Farage acknowledged the revelations 'look bad' but insisted no illegal money was taken.

stories.title: Reform conference: Three crucial questions facing Farage as donations scandal engulfs party
stories.summary: Analysis from BBC outlines three key questions facing Farage: can Reform maintain its momentum, can it survive the donations crisis, and is the party building a genuine political machine? The conference took place amid turbulence from the undercover investigation.

stories.title: Burnham rules out second Scottish independence referendum as 'off limits'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed that a second Scottish independence referendum remains firmly 'off limits' under his government, dashing SNP hopes for a new vote in the current parliamentary term.

stories.title: SNP, Plaid Cymru and Sinn Féin sign memorandum calling for constitutional change
stories.summary: The three Celtic nationalist parties met in Cardiff and signed a joint memorandum calling for constitutional change and greater devolved control, signalling a coordinated push against Westminster's stance on self-determination.

stories.title: Guardian editorial: SNP in need of renewal like Labour
stories.summary: The Guardian argued that Scotland's political landscape is shifting, with the SNP — like Labour — facing an urgent need for internal renewal as its political dominance in Scotland is challenged from multiple directions.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Cabinet Office Annual Report 2025-26 published
stories.summary: The Cabinet Office published its Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26, covering the department's activities under the Starmer government and the early weeks of the Burnham administration, including business appointment rules and senior appointments.

stories.title: Burnham cabinet confirmed: Healey as Chancellor, Haigh as First Secretary
stories.summary: The full Burnham cabinet was confirmed in July 2026: John Healey as Chancellor, Louise Haigh as First Secretary/Cabinet Office, Angela Rayner at MHCLG, Lisa Nandy at Digital/Culture, with Shabana Mahmood remaining as Home Secretary.

stories.title: DSIT staff redistributed as Burnham restructures science and technology portfolio
stories.summary: Following the scrapping of DSIT, the 'majority of DSIT staff' are now in new roles across DBIST, DCMS and the Cabinet Office, with back-office functions still being redistributed as the Burnham government beds in its restructure.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: YouGov poll: Labour and Reform tied at 23%, Conservatives on 20%
stories.summary: The latest YouGov poll (13-14 Sep) shows Labour and Reform UK tied at 23%, with Conservatives on 20%, Lib Dems on 13% and Greens on 11%. The 7-poll moving average puts Labour fractionally ahead at 26% vs Reform on 23.1%.

stories.title: Lib Dems preparing snap election manifesto amid speculation of early poll
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrats have begun work on a new general election manifesto as speculation grows about a possible snap election under PM Burnham, who inherited Labour's diminished parliamentary majority.

stories.title: Reform UK projected to win 132 seats at current polling, says Electoral Calculus
stories.summary: Electoral Calculus modelling based on September 2026 polling projects Reform UK winning 132 seats at the next general election — a dramatic surge from its 5 seats in 2024 — if current trends hold.

stories.title: Two new peers introduced: Lord Leveson and Lord McTague
stories.summary: Former Investigatory Powers Commissioner and press inquiry chair Sir Brian Leveson was introduced as Lord Leveson of Liverpool (Crossbench), and ex-Federation of Small Businesses chair Martin McTague as Lord McTague (Labour), in the week of 14 September.

stories.title: Railways Bill continues Lords committee stage: new technologies and environmental targets debated
stories.summary: The Railways Bill continued its committee stage in the House of Lords, with members discussing amendments relating to new technologies, heritage railways and environmental targets.

stories.title: House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 became law in March
stories.summary: The House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 was passed in March 2026, completing the removal of all remaining hereditary peers from the upper chamber — a long-standing Labour reform commitment.
